headline: Math is nearly saturated while real-world agent work still lags
outlook: Math is the clearest story. It has closed 95% of its remaining headroom over the past year, FrontierMath crossed 90% on September 1, and GPT-6.1 Sol just posted 100% on FrontierMath Tier 4. Agents and real work is the slowest category, with only 34% of headroom closed: the Remote Labor Index sits at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%, though September's run of APEX-Agents records up to 82.2% shows some agent tests are moving quickly. The trend that may matter most for practical work is task length, where Claude Mythos Preview now handles 17.4-hour tasks and the horizon has been doubling roughly every 4.1 months, so on current trends a full 40-hour work-week task most likely arrives around December 2026, with a likely range stretching to August 2027. Meanwhile the tracked price has fallen from $3.44 per million tokens (Gemini 2.5 Pro, March 2025) to $0.055 (Qwen3.7 Flash), but Terminal-Bench and GeoBench running behind trend, and past likely ranges containing the real date only 59% of the time, are reminders that these are extrapolations, not schedules.
